Web confirms Alexis (FH, 2012, 293 units, 356 Alexandra Rd, D03) recent-12mo transactions $1,571-$2,131 psf (avg ~$1,859), with current PSF range $1,433-$2,180 - so $1,433 is the floor of the live range and a genuine discount to the average, supporting the -35.8% age-adj signal at the project level. history.summary: A freehold 635sqft 2BR at Alexis (D03 Queenstown, 480m to Queenstown MRT) asking $1.05M / $1,654 psf. The ask is genuine and fairly priced — ~3% below the project's own same-size 24-month URA prints (median $1,702, n=6, latest Apr-2026 at $1,714 psf) — but it is fair value, not a bargain. The 755 score rests on a 4.8%/yr project CAGR that same-size resale-to-resale evidence contradicts: within this unit's 546-700sqft band, median PSF moved $1,691 (2021-22) to $1,702 (2024H2-2026), roughly 0.2%/yr, while the project-wide 'appreciation' came almost entirely from a mix shift (median transacted size fell 657sqft to 420sqft; shoebox share 46% to 78%). Real carry (~4.1% gross on URA-evidenced rent) and solid downside support, but no credible appreciation case.
history.rating_rationale: PRICED FAIRLY, NOT CHEAPLY. The headline -22.5% vs age-adjusted D03 peers is structural, not opportunity. Against the only comp set that matters — Alexis' own 591-679sqft prints — the ask is just -2.8% (median $1,702, n=6). MMR's own v3.12 low-floor flag fired at stack_low_floor_share = 1.00 (all 6 same-size prints on floors 01-05; Alexis is a 2-block low-rise), which already halved value credit and applied -7; research explains the remaining district gap: the project fronts Alexandra Road with documented resident noise complaints (the developer's own double-glazing on the road-facing side concedes the issue), an 18-21 shop retail podium generating foot traffic and lax security, plus recurring mould/ventilation and maintenance complaints. APPRECIATION INPUT IS A MIX ARTIFACT. Project median PSF rose $1,479 (2021) to $1,870 (2026), +26%, but median transacted size collapsed from 657 to 420sqft over the same period. Band-by-band: 546-700sqft +0.7% total (~0.2%/yr), 350-545sqft shoebox +2.6% (~0.9%/yr). The exact 635sqft layout printed $1,771 psf (Jun-2022) and $1,748 psf (Oct-2023); today's ask is $1,654. This unit's size band has not participated in RCR's move. Overrode 4.8% to 2.5%/yr, which drops all-cash 5yr annualized ROI from 5.6% to ~3.5%. REALSMART CORROBORATES: REALSCORE 2.3/5 on a deep sample (295 matched resale pairs) — bottom-half nationally and well under D3 peers Queens 3.6 and Stirling Residences 4.2 — with avg annualized profit of just 1.7% over the past year. The 90.5% profitable figure (266 vs 29) is real downside evidence, not upside: it mostly reflects owners who entered at 2008-2012 launch or 2020-21 lows. NOT AVOID: freehold, 480m to EW19, a verified-fair ask, ~4.1% gross carry on real URA contracts, a low $1.05M ticket with a wide buyer pool, and 589 lifetime transactions across 293 units give genuine liquidity and downside support. NOT A BUY: strip the mix-artifact CAGR and the floor/quality-driven district discount and nothing is left to pay for the risk — a compact 2BR with a single bathroom, in a project with ~3% of stock listed for sale and ~9.5% on the rental market at once.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Sound but below the modelled figure. The model uses $3,800/mo (ura_project_bed, conf 0.95), but the actual URA contract for a 600-700sqft 2BR at Alexis was $3,600/mo (Jun-2026), and the median across the latest 12 contracts is $3,150 (skewed by the shoebox-heavy mix). At $3,600 the gross yield is ~4.11%, not 4.34% — still respectable carry for a freehold RCR unit at a $1.05M ticket, and realsmart's independent estimate agrees at 4.3% project-wide / $6.60 avg PSF rental on 73 contracts in the past month. Demand drivers are real: 480m to Queenstown MRT, one stop to the CBD corridor, mature amenities. The drag is the single bathroom (couples/singles only, no shared-tenancy premium) and ~28 Alexis units competing on the rental market at once. Expect $3,400-3,700 achievable.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: This is where the listing fails. The 4.8%/yr ura_5yr_cagr is a composition effect, not price growth: Alexis' median transacted size fell from 657sqft (2021) to 420sqft (2026) as shoebox share rose 46% to 78%, mechanically lifting median PSF from $1,479 to $1,870. Measured within size bands, the project has barely moved: 546-700sqft (this unit) $1,691 to $1,702, ~0.2%/yr; 350-545sqft shoebox $1,853 to $1,901, ~0.9%/yr. The exact 635sqft layout transacted at $1,771 psf (Jun-2022) and $1,748 psf (Oct-2023) — today's $1,654 ask is below both, four years on, in a period when RCR as a whole appreciated. Realsmart independently prints avg annualized profit of 1.7% over the past year and a REALSCORE of 2.3/5 across 295 matched pairs. Forward: I set 2.5%/yr — above the project's flat trailing band (trailing CAGR has ~0 forward power, so 0.2% would be its own error) but materially below the RCR 3.7% baseline, because the discount vs district peers is explained by floor mix, the Alexandra Road frontage and the retail podium rather than by mispricing. At 2.5% the all-cash 5yr annualized ROI is ~3.5%, not the 5.6% in the projections.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No profile exists for Alexis (status: not_researched), so this unit's floor and facing are unverified — a real gap, since Alexandra-Road-facing vs inner/pool-facing is the biggest single swing on both noise and rentability here. What the prints do say: all 6 same-size (591-679sqft) 24-month prints are on floors 01-05 and stack_low_floor_share = 1.00. Alexis is a 2-block low-rise, so 01-05 is much of the building rather than a PES artifact — but it does mean the correct comp for this unit is $1,702 psf (its own band's prints), not the $2,135 age-adjusted D03 median. The 2BR/1-bath 635sqft configuration sits at the compact end of the project's 527-1,033sqft 2BR range. Before committing, verify facing (double-glazed road-facing units carry the noise), floor, and whether the unit is above the retail podium.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: URA same-project, same-size resale-to-resale (no new-launch data): Alexis 546-700sqft band median PSF $1,691 (2021-22, n=4) to $1,702 (2024H2-2026, n=6) = ~0.2%/yr; 350-545sqft band $1,853 to $1,901 = ~0.9%/yr; the exact 635sqft layout $1,771 psf (Jun-2022) / $1,748 psf (Oct-2023) vs $1,654 asked now. Corroborated by realsmart avg annualized profit 1.7% (past 1y) and REALSCORE 2.3 on 295 matched pairs. Set at 2.5% rather than the trailing ~0.2% because trailing CAGR has ~0 forward power; 2.5% discounts the RCR 3.7% baseline for a project that demonstrably did not participate in its region's move. Downward override only — no new-launch inflation reintroduced.

history.summary: A 635sqft 2BR/1-bath at Alexis, a 293-unit freehold LOW-RISE mixed development (293 homes + 18 shops) 400-520m from Queenstown MRT, asking $1.05M / $1,654 psf. The carry is genuinely good (a signed Jun-2026 2BR 600-700sqft contract at $3,600/mo = 4.1% gross) and the downside record is deep and protective (realsmart 90.5% profitable on 295 matched pairs, 50+ deals/yr on 293 units). But the ask is at market, not below it, and this unit's own size band is the one band at Alexis that has not participated in the 2021-26 bull market at all - so you are buying carry and liquidity, not an entry discount that re-rates.
history.rating_rationale: The 755 score and the -22.5% 'cheap vs age-adjusted D03 peers' reading both overstate the value case, for two separate reasons I could verify. (1) THE APPRECIATION INPUT IS A MIX ARTIFACT. The 4.8%/yr ura_5yr_cagr over 67 prints is composition, not price growth: Alexis's transacting mix shifted from 900+sqft units (median $1,263psf, 8 prints pre-2023) to sub-550sqft shoeboxes ($1,900-2,100psf, nearly all of 2025-26), with ZERO 900+sqft prints since 2023. Split by size band, the subject's own 590-700sqft band went $1,703 (pre-2023) -> $1,702 (2024+), -0.1%, while shoebox +6.7%, 450-590 +10.9%, 700-900 +9.6%. Exact-size evidence is starker: 635sqft printed $1,771 in Jun-22 and $1,748 in Oct-23 - today's $1,654 ask is BELOW both, four years on. (2) THE DISCOUNT VS D03 PEERS IS STRUCTURAL AND PERMANENT. All 67 URA prints sit on floors 01-10 (52 of 67 on 01-05) because Alexis is low-rise; its D03 comparators (Alex Residences, Stirling Residences, Queens Peak) are high-rise towers. MMR correctly fires stack_low_floor_share>=0.7 (low_floor -7.0, psf_value halved) but still credits +7.94 age_value off that same structural gap - I discount most of it, because a low-rise mixed-use project does not re-rate to tower PSF. Against its OWN tight comps the unit is merely fair: -2.8% vs the six 590-700sqft prints in 24mo (Apr-26 624sqft went at $1,714). Layered on that: documented, specific maintenance failure (mouldy walls, peeling paint, leaking carpark pipes, power/water outages, dead facilities, dormitory-narrow corridors; SingaporeExpats 6.9/10 on 14 reviews) plus workshop and Alexandra Road noise - a credible mechanism for why the band is stuck, since shoebox investors never live there while 600-700sqft 2BR buyers do. A 2BR with ONE bathroom narrows both the tenant and resale pool (livability 47). It is not an Avoid: the ask is at market rather than above it, the yield is real, and 90.5%-profitable on 295 pairs is genuine downside protection. It is simply a fair price for a project whose mid-size stock has gone nowhere. At ~$1,500-1,550psf ($955k-985k) the entry discount would start paying for the maintenance risk; at $1,654 it does not.

agent_evaluation.summary: A 635sqft 2BR/1-bath at Alexis, a 293-unit freehold LOW-RISE mixed development (293 homes + 18 shops) 400-520m from Queenstown MRT, asking $1.05M / $1,654 psf. The carry is genuinely good (a signed Jun-2026 2BR 600-700sqft contract at $3,600/mo = 4.1% gross) and the downside record is deep and protective (realsmart 90.5% profitable on 295 matched pairs, 50+ deals/yr on 293 units). But the ask is at market, not below it, and this unit's own size band is the one band at Alexis that has not participated in the 2021-26 bull market at all - so you are buying carry and liquidity, not an entry discount that re-rates.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: The 755 score and the -22.5% 'cheap vs age-adjusted D03 peers' reading both overstate the value case, for two separate reasons I could verify. (1) THE APPRECIATION INPUT IS A MIX ARTIFACT. The 4.8%/yr ura_5yr_cagr over 67 prints is composition, not price growth: Alexis's transacting mix shifted from 900+sqft units (median $1,263psf, 8 prints pre-2023) to sub-550sqft shoeboxes ($1,900-2,100psf, nearly all of 2025-26), with ZERO 900+sqft prints since 2023. Split by size band, the subject's own 590-700sqft band went $1,703 (pre-2023) -> $1,702 (2024+), -0.1%, while shoebox +6.7%, 450-590 +10.9%, 700-900 +9.6%. Exact-size evidence is starker: 635sqft printed $1,771 in Jun-22 and $1,748 in Oct-23 - today's $1,654 ask is BELOW both, four years on. (2) THE DISCOUNT VS D03 PEERS IS STRUCTURAL AND PERMANENT. All 67 URA prints sit on floors 01-10 (52 of 67 on 01-05) because Alexis is low-rise; its D03 comparators (Alex Residences, Stirling Residences, Queens Peak) are high-rise towers. MMR correctly fires stack_low_floor_share>=0.7 (low_floor -7.0, psf_value halved) but still credits +7.94 age_value off that same structural gap - I discount most of it, because a low-rise mixed-use project does not re-rate to tower PSF. Against its OWN tight comps the unit is merely fair: -2.8% vs the six 590-700sqft prints in 24mo (Apr-26 624sqft went at $1,714). Layered on that: documented, specific maintenance failure (mouldy walls, peeling paint, leaking carpark pipes, power/water outages, dead facilities, dormitory-narrow corridors; SingaporeExpats 6.9/10 on 14 reviews) plus workshop and Alexandra Road noise - a credible mechanism for why the band is stuck, since shoebox investors never live there while 600-700sqft 2BR buyers do. A 2BR with ONE bathroom narrows both the tenant and resale pool (livability 47). It is not an Avoid: the ask is at market rather than above it, the yield is real, and 90.5%-profitable on 295 pairs is genuine downside protection. It is simply a fair price for a project whose mid-size stock has gone nowhere. At ~$1,500-1,550psf ($955k-985k) the entry discount would start paying for the maintenance risk; at $1,654 it does not.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: The strongest part of this listing. Alexis is a proven rental machine - 73 contracts in the past month alone, avg $6.60 psf, realsmart's estimated yield 4.3%. For this exact band a 2BR 600-700sqft signed at $3,600/mo on 1 Jun 2026, and a live 635sqft 2BR/1-bath is asking $3,900. I use $3,600 as the defensible number (the DB's $3,800 is at the top of plausible; the $6.60 avg psf is inflated by shoeboxes leasing at ~$7.65 psf). That gives 4.11% gross / ~2.9% net - genuinely good for RCR. Demand is MRT-and-CBD-access driven and should hold. Two caveats: the single bathroom rules out unrelated co-tenants sharing, which is the main 2BR rental use case at this size; and Penrith (462u) plus Margaret Drive Residences add competing stock on completion inside the hold window. Per the backtest priors, count this yield as CARRY only - high gross yield predicts LOWER forward price growth (std_beta -0.16), and Alexis's own history is exactly that pattern.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: I override the 4.8%/yr data rate down to 2.5%/yr on resale-to-resale evidence within the subject's own size band. The 4.8% is a Simpson's-paradox mix effect, not price growth: the pooled project median rose $1,479psf (2021) -> $1,870psf (2026) purely because the transacting mix moved from 900+sqft units at ~$1,263psf to sub-550sqft shoeboxes at $1,900-2,100psf, with no 900+sqft print since 2023. Band-by-band over the same window: shoebox <450sqft +6.7%, 450-590 +10.9%, 700-900 +9.6%, and the subject's 590-700sqft band -0.1% ($1,703 -> $1,702). The exact-size series is the cleanest read available: 635sqft at $1,771psf (Jun-22), $1,748psf (Oct-23), and now asking $1,654psf. Four years of a strong bull market produced nothing here. Corroborated independently by realsmart's REALSCORE 2.3/5 and 1.7% avg annualized profit over the past year, and by MMR momentum -0.875. I do not go to zero - four years is a short window, Jun-22 was the band's local peak, and RCR's realized forward baseline is ~3.1%/yr - so 2.5%/yr is my haircut for the demonstrated structural drag. At 2.5% appreciation and $3,600 rent the all-cash 5yr annualized ROI is ~3.5% (vs the run's 5.56% at the unadjusted rate): positive, but thin compensation for a project with this maintenance record.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No researched profile exists for Alexis (stack_profile: not_researched) and the listing discloses neither floor nor facing - but the ceiling is low either way. Every one of the 67 URA prints at Alexis is on floors 01-10, with 52 of 67 on 01-05: this is a low-rise mixed development (293 homes over 18 shops), so there is no high-floor or view stock to aspire to and little floor premium to capture. That is why stack_low_floor_share>=0.7 fires here as a property of the WHOLE development rather than of one bad stack - and why I treat the -22.5% gap to age-adjusted D03 peers (all high-rise towers) as permanent rather than as an entry discount. The material unknowns that remain are facing and condition: rear-facing units catch workshop noise, Alexandra Road-facing units catch traffic noise, and residents report mould in units. Any of those would move the call - worth confirming on a viewing before acting, and worth running /research-development on Alexis if the owner wants to transact here.

The pooled 4.8%/yr ura_5yr_cagr is a size-mix artifact (mix moved from 900+sqft at $1,263psf to shoeboxes at $1,900-2,100psf; no 900+sqft print since 2023). 2.5% = RCR realized forward baseline (~3.1%) haircut for the band's demonstrated non-participation; corroborated by realsmart REALSCORE 2.3 and 1.7% avg annualized profit past 1y.
